q: A current of $0.50\,\text{A}$ arrives at a junction. Two branches leave the junction, and the current in one of them is $0.35\,\text{A}$. How large is the current in the other branch?
a: By the current law the sum of the leaving currents is $0.50\,\text{A}$, so the current in the other branch is $0.50\,\text{A} - 0.35\,\text{A} = 0.15\,\text{A}$.

q: A series connection has a $9.0\,\text{V}$ voltage source and three resistors. The voltages of two resistors are $2.0\,\text{V}$ and $3.5\,\text{V}$. How large is the voltage of the third resistor?
a: By the voltage law the voltages of the resistors are together the voltage of the source, so the voltage of the third resistor is $9.0\,\text{V} - 2.0\,\text{V} - 3.5\,\text{V} = 3.5\,\text{V}$.
